page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c4.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8369HB processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server is configured with 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores, operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. It includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-focused allocation of 2.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.c4.4xlarge in the average performance tier across most compute workloads. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a single-core Geekbench score of 1253.0 and a multi-core score of 7455.0, supported by advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration via AES. In data processing tests, the instance demonstrates a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 26.96 GB/sec and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 77.01 GB/sec. However, memory performance is a relative bottleneck, with the Passmark memory score falling into the weak category, though cached small-block read bandwidth remains high at 921.81 GB/sec.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, the ecs.c4.4xlarge offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for software compilation, web serving, and moderate database operations, as evidenced by its 9.51 GB/sec static web serving throughput and 15.83 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. It can also handle lightweight machine learning tasks, processing 135M parameter LLM prompts at 991.37 tokens per second, though performance drops significantly on larger models.
